verses.text: Honor fits a fool about as well as snow fits summer or rain fits harvest.
An undeserved curse is like a sparrow fluttering or a swallow darting past. It doesn't land.
A whip is for a horse, a bridle for a donkey, and a rod for the backs of fools.
Don't answer a fool on their own foolish terms, or you'll become just like them.
Answer a fool in a way that exposes the foolishness, or they'll think they're wise.
Sending a message with a fool is like cutting off your own feet and drinking down violence.
A proverb in a fool's mouth is like legs hanging limp and useless.
Honoring a fool is like tying a stone into a sling.
A proverb in a fool's mouth is like a thornbush in a drunk person's hand.
Hiring a fool or just anyone passing by is like an archer who wounds whoever's around.
A fool repeats their foolishness like a dog going back to its vomit.
See someone who thinks they're already wise? There's more hope for a fool than for them.
A slacker says, “There's a lion in the road! A fierce lion is roaming the streets!”
A slacker turns over in bed like a door swinging on its hinges.
A slacker sticks their hand in the dish and is too lazy to bring the food to their mouth.
A slacker thinks they're wiser than seven people who answer with good judgment.
Jumping into someone else's fight is like grabbing a dog by the ears.
Like someone out of control firing flaming torches and deadly arrows
is the person who tricks their neighbor and says, “I was just joking!”
Without wood, a fire goes out. Without gossip, a fight dies down. 🔥
A person who loves to argue stirs up conflict like coal feeds hot embers and wood feeds a fire.
Gossip goes down like tasty bites, all the way into a person's deepest parts.
Passionate words from an evil heart are like silver dross coating a clay pot.
A malicious person hides who they are with their words while keeping evil in their heart.
When they sound charming, don't believe them. There are seven detestable things in their heart.
They may hide their malice with lies, but their wickedness will come out in front of everyone.
Dig a pit and you'll fall into it. Roll a stone and it'll roll back on you.
A lying tongue hates the people it hurts, and flattery brings ruin.
